newsitem.title: USA: Dole chides Clinton on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Dole chides Clinton on Iraq.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole on Monday chided President Bill Clinton for claiming success in the latest showdown with Iraq, saying "events on the ground" contradict the statement.
Saying the "credibility of the United States is at stake," Dole challenged Clinton's claim that the cruise missile strikes he ordered last week had achieved their purpose.

Citing "reports of continued strife and killings in Northern Iraq -- to include executions of U.S. backed Iraqi opposition personnel ... and the lack of evidence of an Iraqi withdrawal from the North," Dole voiced doubt about the mission's success.
He said in a statement such developments "raise questions about whether the administration's strategy has advanced U.S. interests in the region."

"The Clinton administration should be careful about making claims of success that events on the ground may not substantiate, and about giving assurances that it is unable or unwilling to fulfil, because the credibility of the United States is at stake," he said.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry dismissed Dole's statement, saying, "The former senator is, unfortunately, attempting to make politics out of an international crisis that the president as commander-in-chief is dealing with and dealing with effectively.
"Mr. Dole, I think, has misjudged the situation," he said.
